messages:
maria (Support): Customer BA-293 opened a billing ticket — invoice jumped from $23 -> $154 this cycle. They say our JS SDK estimator reports ~18.2k tokens but invoice lists ~26.6k. Can we triage?
kevin (SRE): request id? sdk version? any quick repro? :eyes:
maria (Support): req_0a1b2c3d, sdk js 0.9.4. Customer provided a short repro and logs. Snippet they used: 
```js
const res = await client.chat.completions.create({
  model: 'rwkv-13b',
  messages: [
    {role: 'system', content: 'You are concise'},
    {role: 'user', content: '<<~8k token prompt payload~>>'}
  ],
  stream: true,
  functions: [{name: 'summarize', /* ... */}]
});
```
maria (Support): Local estimator output: prompt: 3,200 tokens, completion: 15,040 tokens -> total 18,240. Invoice shows prompt 3,200, completion 23,378 -> delta ~8,138 tokens.
sam (ML Eng): hmm, that smells like a server-side pass that ran after the streamed completion (post-run tool / summarizer) and got counted in metering. Does the customer see a final appended message or extra bytes in the final completion?
maria (Support): customer says yes — they see an extra "assistant" message with a long summary appended after stream end. SDK estimator stops at the streamed content and doesn't include that postrun.
kevin (SRE): can you paste the curl they used or the full response? we need to see whether postrun is happening inside our runtime or an external tool call.
maria (Support): curl payload they sent: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"rwkv-13b","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are concise"},{"role":"user","content":"<<big prompt>>"}],"functions":[{"name":"summarize"}],"stream":true}'
```
Also attached: the final wire response includes a separate event with role:assistant and a long content block labelled "postrun_summary_v1".
ara (Billing): opened billing case BI-842 and flagged for metering audit. I'll pull the invoice lines and link them to req_0a1b2c3d.
jamie (Client SDK): note: SDK estimator in 0.9.4 intentionally counts only messages emitted to the client during streaming; it does not (and cannot) see server-internal postrun messages that get appended before finalizing the bill. We added a warning in 0.9.6 release notes about server postrun tokens.
maria (Support): customer insists they saw the postrun summary in the response body (so it was visible), but the estimator still undercounted. They think SDK didn't include server-appended messages when computing pre-bill estimate.
sam (ML Eng): likely flow: 1) stream tokens forwarded to client (counted by estimator), 2) runtime invokes summarizer function (server-side) producing additional tokens, 3) runtime appends the summary to final response and meters it. Estimator misses (2). We should confirm whether summarizer executed on same request path or as async job.
kevin (SRE): quick repro options: ask customer to retry with header `x-rw-postrun: false` to disable server postrun, or run with `stream: false` so estimator sees final combined output. That will tell us if postrun is the delta.
maria (Support): passed workaround to customer. They will test and report back. :thumbsup:
metering-bot: metering audit note: invoice for req_0a1b2c3d shows total_tokens=26578, flagged for BI-842.
ara (Billing): if audit shows tokens were not documented in estimator, we may need to adjust the invoice or clarify billing docs. Holding until SRE/ML confirms root cause.
jamie (Client SDK): longer-term: we can change estimator to fetch the final server restatement or provide a "finalized response hint" webhook when available. For now document as known limitation for SDK <=0.9.4.
kevin (SRE): action items: (1) SRE to pull full runtime trace for req_0a1b2c3d including internal function call footprints; (2) ML to confirm whether summarizer is invoked synchronously and tokenized by metering; (3) Billing to keep customer case open and hold adjustments pending audit.
sam (ML Eng): assigning to me for analysis, will try to reproduce with a synthetic 9k prompt + function hook. ETA EOD.
maria (Support): thanks everyone — I shared recon steps and the customer's logs. Will update the thread when customer tests the header toggle. :ok_hand:
